title: Transmitting controlled-substance prescriptions to a central fill pharmacy and the records each side keeps
rule_summary: Under 21 CFR 1306.15 (Schedule II) and 21 CFR 1306.27 (Schedules III, IV and V) a retail pharmacy may provide prescription information to an authorized central fill pharmacy for dispensing purposes, and may transmit the prescriptions electronically, including via facsimile. The transmitting retail pharmacy must write the words "CENTRAL FILL" on the face of the original prescription (1306.15(a)(1) says the original paper prescription) and record the name, address and DEA registration number of the central fill pharmacy, the name of the retail pharmacy pharmacist transmitting the prescription, and the date of transmittal; for an electronic Schedule II prescription, 1306.15(a)(1) requires that information to be added to the electronic prescription record. It must ensure that all information required on a prescription by 21 CFR 1306.05 is transmitted; for Schedules III-V it must also indicate the number of refills already dispensed and the number remaining. It must maintain the original prescription for two years from the date the prescription was filled (Schedule II) or last refilled (Schedules III-V), and keep a record of receipt of the filled prescription, including the date of receipt, the method of delivery (private, common or contract carrier) and the name of the retail pharmacy employee accepting delivery. The central fill pharmacy must keep a copy of the prescription (if sent via facsimile) or an electronic record of all information transmitted, including the name, address and DEA registration number of the transmitting retail pharmacy; a record of the date of receipt, the name of the pharmacist (for Schedules III-V, the licensed pharmacist) filling the prescription, and the date of filling (for Schedules III-V, dates of filling or refilling); and a record of the date the filled prescription was delivered to the retail pharmacy and the method of delivery.
exam_relevance: Tests which pharmacy keeps which central fill record, the refill information added for Schedules III-V, and the different events from which the two-year retention of the original prescription runs.

authority.name: Provision of prescription information between retail pharmacies and central fill pharmacies for prescriptions of Schedule II controlled substances

numeric_facts.fact: retail pharmacy retention of the original Schedule II prescription sent for central fill
numeric_facts.conditions: from the date the prescription was filled; 21 CFR 1306.15(a)(3)

numeric_facts.fact: retail pharmacy retention of the original Schedule III-V prescription sent for central fill
numeric_facts.conditions: from the date the prescription was last refilled; 21 CFR 1306.27(a)(4)

common_confusions: The words "CENTRAL FILL" are written by the transmitting retail pharmacy, not by the central fill pharmacy.
The retail pharmacy records who accepted delivery of the filled prescription; the central fill pharmacy records when and how it delivered it.
